name: 1 Chronicles
tagline: Israel’s story retold for the returned exiles
author: Not named in the text. Tradition names Ezra.
date: Written after the exile, probably in the 400s or 300s BC.
setting: Written to people who had returned from exile and were rebuilding their identity.
theme: God’s covenant with David and the worship of the temple remain at the center of his people’s hope.

outline.label: Genealogies from Adam to the exile
The tribe of Judah and the house of David
From Saul’s death to David’s rise
The ark and the blessing on Obed-edom
The procession and the psalm of thanks
The promise of an eternal house

christInBook: The Chronicler holds the covenant with David at the center, a promise that the Messiah would come from David’s line. The temple preparations point toward the final dwelling of God with his people.
howToRead: Chronicles retells Israel’s history from the viewpoint of the returned exiles. Read the opening genealogies as a statement that God’s people have a name, a place, and a future.
